# Glossary terms

Published writing reuses a small set of load-bearing terms, and each one means
exactly one thing everywhere it appears. A reader who meets the same word with two
meanings in two posts concludes the company is imprecise about its own subject.

**Pipeline** means a customer's end-to-end analytics data flow, from source system to
consumable output. It never means our internal delivery process; that is "the
delivery workflow" wherever it must be mentioned.

**Incident** means a customer-visible failure with a start and an end. Degradations
that customers never saw are "internal failures" and are labeled as such, because
inflating them into incidents makes real incidents unremarkable.

**Finding** means a checkable statement produced by reviewing evidence. Opinions,
however well-informed, are labeled as positions. The distinction carries the whole
evidence-standards structure and is never blurred for rhythm.

**Reliability** is used only with a stated measurement basis. Naked "more reliable"
is a banned comparative; "fewer failed runs per thousand over the measured quarter"
survives review.

**Practitioner** means someone who personally operates the systems under discussion.
Managers of practitioners are "team leads"; the distinction decides which audience
depth a piece is written for.

New recurring terms are added here at first published use, with the definition the
first use committed to. Retiring or redefining a term is an editorial decision made
once, recorded here, never improvised per post.

## Enforcement

Reviews check glossary conformance mechanically: a term used off-definition is a
blocking structure comment with this guideline cited, so the discussion happens at
the definition — where it is settled once — rather than per draft. Writers proposing
a better definition propose it here, not in a draft that quietly uses it.
